newsitem.title: USA: US muni groups call yield burning unfunded mandate.
newsitem.headline: US muni groups call yield burning unfunded mandate.

text.p: Muni bond groups warned a top U.S. Treasury Department official on Monday that the agency's "yield burning" plan has a significant fiscal impact on state and local governments.
The plan would, therefore, violate a law against unfunded federal mandates. It would also violate a White House order on intergovernmental relations, a group spokesman said.

Mark Schwartz, president of the National League of Cities, made the statement at a press briefing following the first-ever meeting between muni groups and Donald Lubick, Treasury's assistant secretary for tax policy.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond refinancing deals.

The IRS last year surprised localities with a plan that says issuers can avoid having interest on the bonds declared taxable by paying Treasury the difference between the price they paid and the spot price of the securities on purhcase date, plus interest.

But a half dozen issuer groups told Lubick today that the IRS' 1996 plan on yield burning, called a "revenue procedure," violates the Unfunded Federal Mandates Reform Act of 1995 and the President's Executive Order 12975 called "Enhancing the Intergovernmental Partnership," Schwartz said.

He said the groups today repeated concerns raised in a January 14 letter to Lubick. The letter says the revenue procedure constitutes an "unfunded federal mandate on state and local taxpayers, a duplicative form of federal regulation, and a threat to state and local taxpayers."
A spokesman for Lubick said the assistant secretary was not available to comment.
